articles.title: Full Story Behind Safaricom’s Sacking of 118 Employees Over Fraud
articles.summary: Safaricom has disclosed that it dismissed 118 officials over fraud-related cases during the financial year that ended in March 2026, while M-Pesa processed...
articles.body:
Safaricom has disclosed that it dismissed 118 officials over fraud-related cases during the financial year that ended in March 2026, while M-Pesa processed transactions worth KSh 41.68 trillion over the same period.

The details are contained in the telecommunications firm's Business and Sustainability Report for the 2025/2026 financial year, which outlines the company's response to fraud, disciplinary measures taken against employees and the scale of transactions processed through its mobile money platform.

According to the report, Safaricom issued three disciplinary warnings and referred 14 cases to law enforcement agencies for further action. The dismissals formed part of the company's measures to address fraud-related incidents and strengthen accountability within its operations.

The report also indicates that Safaricom recorded an 82 per cent reduction in fraud-related cases, against a target of 90 per cent. However, the company reportedly recovered 46 per cent of the items or assets reported lost, highlighting the continuing challenges associated with fraud prevention and recovery.

Beyond the fraud disclosures, the report provides an indication of the scale of financial activity taking place through M-Pesa, one of Kenya's most widely used mobile money platforms.

During the financial year under review, M-Pesa processed approximately 46.4 billion transactions, with the total value reaching KSh 41.68 trillion. The figures underscore the platform's central role in Kenya's financial ecosystem, where individuals and businesses rely on mobile money for payments, transfers and other financial services.

The disclosures offer insight into Safaricom's efforts to combat fraud while managing the enormous volume of financial transactions passing through its systems. They also highlight the importance of internal controls, accountability and cooperation with law enforcement in protecting customers and the company from fraud-related risks.

articles.title: Kenya’s Public Universities Remain Shut as UASU Rejects Sh11 Billion Government Offer
articles.summary: Academic activities in public universities across Kenya remain paralysed following the collapse of the third meeting between the Universities Academic Staff...
articles.body:
Academic activities in public universities across Kenya remain paralysed following the collapse of the third meeting between the Universities Academic Staff Union (UASU) and the government over the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA).

The government reportedly offered KSh 11 billion, but UASU officials rejected the proposal, describing it as vague and insufficient to address the rising cost of living and inflation. The union maintains that at least KSh 12 billion is required to resolve the dispute and pave the way for the resumption of academic activities.

UASU further stated that no negotiations had taken place since the strike began on November 2, 2026. The union is now demanding immediate negotiations, the signing and registration of the 2025–2029 CBA, and its full implementation before normal university operations can resume.

As the standoff continues, students remain among the hardest hit. Many are still required to pay rent and cater for daily expenses despite the disruption of their studies. At the University of Nairobi, some students staged protests, blocking sections of Waiyaki Way to express their frustration over the prolonged shutdown. During the demonstrations, student leaders called on the Cabinet Secretary for Education to resign, accusing him of failing to resolve the crisis and safeguard students' academic interests.

With the two sides yet to reach an agreement, uncertainty continues to surround the reopening of universities, leaving thousands of students waiting for a resolution to the dispute.

articles.title: Manchester United at a Crossroads: Will Bournemouth Clash Decide Michael Carrick’s Future?
articles.summary:
By Vanywinner KE | October 25, 2026

Manchester United are facing another difficult period, with growing questions about the team's performances and the future
articles.body:
By Vanywinner KE | October 25, 2026

Manchester United are facing another difficult period, with growing questions about the team's performances and the future of manager Michael Carrick. As the club prepares to face Bournemouth, attention is shifting from the results on the pitch to a bigger question: does Carrick still have what it takes to lead United's recovery?

For a club with Manchester United's history and ambitions, poor results rarely remain a purely sporting issue. They quickly trigger debate among supporters, speculation in the media and questions about whether those in charge need to make significant changes.

However, amid the growing noise surrounding Old Trafford, it is important to separate what has been reported from what remains unconfirmed.

The pressure is mounting at Old Trafford

United's recent run of disappointing performances has intensified scrutiny of Carrick. The reported heavy defeat against Como has added to concerns about the team's defensive organisation, tactical approach and ability to compete consistently.

The problem is not simply losing a match. Supporters want to see evidence that the team is progressing, that players understand their roles and that the manager has a workable plan for difficult situations.

When disappointing results continue, confidence becomes harder to maintain. Every tactical decision attracts attention, every substitution invites debate and every subsequent fixture becomes an opportunity for the manager to prove that the situation can be turned around.

For Carrick, the Bournemouth match arrives at a particularly sensitive moment.

Is Manchester United preparing to sack Carrick?

Speculation about a possible managerial change has become a major talking point. Several reports have suggested that Carrick's position is under pressure and that the club could reconsider its options if results fail to improve.

Nevertheless, there is an important difference between a manager facing uncertainty and a club having made a final decision to dismiss him.

As of October 25, reports indicated that Carrick was expected to lead United against Bournemouth. There was no confirmed announcement establishing that he had been dismissed.

This means supporters should be cautious about claims circulating online that suggest his departure is already settled. Unless Manchester United or a reliable source confirms a decision, reports about an imminent sacking should be treated as speculation rather than established fact.

The club's silence, where applicable, should not automatically be interpreted as evidence that a dismissal is being planned.

Why the Bournemouth match matters

The meeting with Bournemouth offers United an opportunity to respond on the pitch rather than through statements or rumours.

A convincing victory could ease some of the pressure on Carrick and provide evidence that the players remain capable of executing his plans. More importantly, a good performance could give the team renewed confidence ahead of its next fixtures.

A disappointing result, on the other hand, would intensify questions about whether the current approach is producing meaningful progress.

Even then, one result would not necessarily determine Carrick's future. Club executives would need to consider the wider pattern of performances, the team's league position, the quality of play and whether there is a realistic alternative capable of improving matters.

For United, the challenge is to turn the match into the beginning of a recovery rather than another isolated result.

Who could replace Carrick?

Names such as Unai Emery and Julian Nagelsmann have been mentioned in discussions about possible alternatives. Antonio Conte has also featured in managerial speculation.

Their reputations and experience make them natural subjects of debate whenever a major club faces uncertainty in the dugout. However, being linked with a vacancy does not establish that a manager has been approached, that negotiations are taking place or that an appointment is imminent.

Any serious replacement decision would involve more than selecting a famous name. United would need to consider tactical compatibility, recruitment priorities, the existing squad and the manager's willingness to work within the club's structure.

A change could provide a fresh start, but it would not automatically resolve every problem affecting the team.

## The deeper question: What kind of Manchester United does the club want?

The uncertainty surrounding Carrick points towards a wider issue that extends beyond the manager.

United need a clear footballing direction. Recruitment must support the intended style of play, players must understand their responsibilities and the club's leadership must assess progress against realistic, consistent objectives.

Repeatedly changing managers without addressing structural weaknesses can create another cycle of rebuilding. A new coach may initially improve results, but lasting progress requires coordination between the manager, recruitment department and club executives.

If Carrick stays, he must demonstrate that he can restore consistency and build a team capable of meeting the club's expectations. If United decide to appoint someone else, the replacement must be given a coherent mandate rather than being expected to solve every problem immediately.

Either path demands accountability and a long-term plan.

What happens next?

Three broad possibilities remain open.

Carrick could use the Bournemouth fixture to begin rebuilding confidence and strengthen his position. United could improve their results while questions about their performances continue. Alternatively, further setbacks could increase the likelihood of a managerial change.

At this stage, these are possibilities, not confirmed outcomes.

The most useful indicators will be the team's performances over the coming matches, the club's official communications and credible reporting about any concrete decisions made by its leadership.

Verdict: Pressure is real, but a sacking is not a confirmed fact

Manchester United's struggles have created genuine uncertainty around Michael Carrick. The team's performances have invited criticism, and the Bournemouth fixture represents an important opportunity to respond.

But supporters and readers should distinguish between a manager being under pressure and a club officially ending his tenure.

Until a dismissal is confirmed, claims that Carrick has been sacked or that a replacement has already been appointed should not be presented as fact.

United's immediate priority is to improve on the pitch. Their longer-term challenge is to build a team and a footballing structure capable of delivering consistent results.

For Carrick, the coming fixtures could prove decisive. For Manchester United, however, the bigger test is whether the club can turn another period of uncertainty into a genuine and sustainable recovery.

Vanywinner KE will continue to follow developments at Old Trafford, separating confirmed news from speculation as the situation unfolds.

articles.title: US Green Card Lottery Faces Fresh Uncertainty as Lawmakers Push to Scrap Programme
articles.summary:
By Vanywinner News | October 24, 2026

Thousands of people hoping to relocate to the United States through the Green Card Lottery are facing fresh uncertainty f
articles.body:
By Vanywinner News | October 24, 2026

Thousands of people hoping to relocate to the United States through the Green Card Lottery are facing fresh uncertainty following a court battle over the delayed 2027 registration period and new efforts by US lawmakers to abolish the programme.

The developments have attracted attention among prospective immigrants in Kenya and across Africa, where the Diversity Visa Lottery offers an opportunity to pursue permanent residence in the United States without necessarily having an employer or close family member sponsor their application.

However, the programme has not been abolished. A federal court has ordered the US government to resume the process, while the administration challenges that decision and some lawmakers seek to end the lottery through legislation.

Court Orders US Government to Reopen Lottery

The latest legal developments follow the failure of the US Department of State to open registration for the 2027 Diversity Visa Programme on its usual schedule.

The department had indicated in November 2025 that changes were being made to the entry process, with registration dates to be announced later. The registration period subsequently remained closed, prompting legal action against the government.

On October 14, 2026, US District Judge Jinsook Ohta issued a preliminary injunction directing the State Department to proceed with the delayed programme. The court later revised the implementation deadlines.

Under the revised order, the department must announce the registration schedule by October 29, 2026, and open registration by November 1. The registration window is required to remain open for 30 days, while selected entrants are to be notified by December 3.

The order also requires the department to process eligible applications within the applicable legal framework and visa allocation.

The ruling followed a lawsuit filed by Red Eagle Law, which challenged the prolonged delay and argued that the government could not effectively suspend a programme established under federal law without adequate legal justification.

The court's intervention does not mean registration is already open. Prospective applicants must wait for the official instructions and confirm the dates published by the State Department.

Source: [Fragomen immigration law update](https://www.fragomen.com/insights/united-states-court-orders-state-department-to-open-fy-2027-diversity-visa-lottery-registration.html).

## Trump Administration Appeals Court Decision

The legal battle is not over.

The US government has appealed the ruling and separately sought to suspend the court order while the appeal proceeds.

The appeal raises questions about the government's obligations under the existing immigration law and the court's authority to compel the department to reopen registration after the normal timetable had been disrupted.

If a court grants the government's request to suspend the order, the deadlines could be affected. If the order remains in force, the department will be expected to comply with the revised timetable unless another court decision changes the situation.

As of October 24, 2026, the available reports indicate that the government has filed its appeal and requested a stay. The latest ruling on that request should be confirmed before publication.

The legal uncertainty means prospective applicants should avoid treating the announced deadlines as completely settled until the government publishes its official registration instructions.

Source: [Report on the government's appeal](https://usimmigration.today/news/state-department-appeals-the-2027-diversity-visa-ruling-and-asks-the-court-to-pause-it/).

## US Congressman Introduces Bill to End Green Card Lottery

As the court dispute continues, a US lawmaker has introduced legislation seeking to terminate the Diversity Visa Programme.

Representative Keith Self, a Republican from Texas, announced the introduction of House Resolution 10896, commonly referred to as H.R. 10896, on October 22, 2026.

The bill seeks to end the diversity immigrant visa lottery. It was subsequently referred to the House Judiciary Committee for consideration.

In announcing the proposal, Self criticised the court ruling requiring the administration to continue the programme and argued that immigration policy should prioritise US national interests and security.

The proposal adds to the ongoing debate over the future of the lottery, which has faced criticism from some political leaders who favour a different approach to selecting immigrants.

However, the bill remains a proposal. It has not become law, and its introduction does not automatically cancel the ongoing legal process or prevent prospective applicants from participating if registration opens under the existing programme.

For the bill to change federal law, it must proceed through the required legislative process. Its eventual impact will depend on whether it advances through Congress and is enacted.

Source: [Representative Keith Self's official announcement](https://keithself.house.gov/media/press-releases/congressman-keith-self-introduces-bill-repeal-diversity-immigration-visa).

## Other Proposals Also Target the Programme

H.R. 10896 is not the only legislative proposal seeking to change the US immigration system by eliminating the lottery.

Another proposal, the SMARTER Act, was introduced by Representative David Schweikert in September 2026. Its provisions include eliminating the Diversity Visa Programme as part of a broader proposed immigration overhaul.

The proposal seeks to move towards a more skills-focused immigration system and make other changes to family-sponsored immigration.

These efforts reflect a broader political debate over whether the United States should continue using a lottery to allocate some permanent residence opportunities or replace it with a system that places greater emphasis on employment skills and other selection criteria.

Nevertheless, the existence of several proposals does not mean the programme is about to disappear. Each bill must be assessed according to its legislative progress, and none should be described as law unless it has completed the required process.

## Why the Green Card Lottery Matters to Kenyans

The Diversity Visa Programme provides an opportunity for eligible people from countries with historically low levels of immigration to the United States to apply for permanent residence.

The programme makes up to 55,000 diversity immigrant visas available annually under its statutory framework, although other legal provisions can reduce the number available in a particular year.

Unlike some employment-based immigration routes, the lottery does not generally require an applicant to obtain a job offer from a US employer before entering.

Applicants must, however, meet the programme's education or work-experience requirements, satisfy the applicable country and other eligibility rules, and complete the required immigration procedures.

For Kenyans hoping to relocate, the current developments raise two separate questions: whether the delayed 2027 registration period will open as ordered by the court, and whether Congress will eventually change the law governing the programme.

The answers will depend on the outcome of the legal proceedings, the official registration announcement and the progress of any legislation introduced in Congress.

Will the Lottery Be Cancelled?

The possibility of future abolition cannot be ruled out, because Congress can amend the law governing the programme. However, a proposal to end the lottery is not the same as a final decision to abolish it.

For now, the court's order and the proposed legislation are separate matters. The court dispute concerns the administration of the programme under the existing legal framework, while lawmakers are considering whether that framework should be changed.

Anyone claiming that the Green Card Lottery has already been permanently abolished should therefore provide evidence of an enacted law or another legally effective decision.

Similarly, applicants should not assume that the court ruling guarantees that registration will proceed without further delays, given the pending appeal.

Warning to Applicants: Avoid Green Card Scams

The uncertainty surrounding the programme may create opportunities for fraudsters to target people eager to move to the United States.

Prospective applicants should be cautious of individuals claiming to have inside information, offering guaranteed selection or demanding payment in exchange for a promise of winning.

The US Department of State advises applicants to use its official Diversity Visa website and to be careful when dealing with intermediaries. Selection in the lottery is not a guarantee of a visa or permanent residence.

The official entry website is https://dvprogram.state.gov/. Applicants should use it only when registration is officially open and follow the instructions issued for the relevant programme year.

Readers should also consult the US Department of State's official immigration guidance at https://travel.state.gov/ for updates on eligibility, application requirements and registration dates.

 What Happens Next?

The immediate developments to watch are the outcome of the government's request to suspend the court order, the official announcement of registration dates and any further action on legislation seeking to abolish the programme.

For Kenyan applicants, the most important message is that the Green Card Lottery has not been permanently abolished by the introduction of H.R. 10896. At the same time, the court's order does not remove the possibility of further legal delays.

Until the situation becomes clearer, prospective applicants should prepare their documents, follow official announcements and avoid making financial commitments based on unverified claims.

The coming weeks could be significant for people hoping to enter the 2027 lottery, as developments in both the courts and Congress may shape the programme's immediate future.

articles.title: Trump Clashes With Independent Journalist During Heated White House Exchange
articles.summary: **WASHINGTON, D.C.** — US President Donald Trump had a tense exchange with Andrew Feinberg, a White House correspondent for *The Independent*, on Tuesday, Octob
articles.body:
**WASHINGTON, D.C.** — US President Donald Trump had a tense exchange with Andrew Feinberg, a White House correspondent for *The Independent*, on Tuesday, October 20, after the journalist raised questions about a proposed government programme targeting fraud.

The confrontation occurred during an Oval Office event where the administration announced a $25 million fund designed to encourage Americans to report fraudulent activities.

According to media reports, Feinberg questioned why the proposed whistleblower programme offered a 1% commission when the federal False Claims Act provides for rewards that can reach at least 10% of the money recovered in qualifying cases.

Trump responded with a warning, telling the journalist to “be careful.” The remark attracted attention as the discussion between the president and the reporter became increasingly tense.

## Trump Interrupts Questions About His Golf Courses

The disagreement continued when Feinberg attempted to raise a separate question concerning Trump's golf courses.

Trump challenged the journalist, asking, “Are you a sick person?” before cutting him off without allowing him to finish his question.

The incident was subsequently reported by several news organisations, including *Newsweek* and *The Wrap*.

Feinberg later addressed the confrontation on X, explaining that he had introduced himself to Trump less than five minutes before the exchange took place.

Because the president interrupted him, the full question about the golf courses was not completed publicly. The available reporting therefore does not establish the complete wording of the question Feinberg intended to ask.

## JD Vance Criticises the Journalist

Vice President JD Vance also commented on the incident after sharing a video clip of the confrontation.

According to media reports, Vance criticised Feinberg's conduct and described the journalist's question as dishonest, aligning himself with the administration's criticism of the exchange.

The incident prompted different interpretations of what had happened. Trump and his supporters questioned the journalist's approach, while the president's response attracted attention as another example of the strained relationship between his administration and sections of the news media.

The controversy grew further after the White House Rapid Response account reportedly published a post containing an offensive slur referring to people with Down syndrome, according to *The Daily Beast*. Reports said the identity of the person responsible for the post had not been publicly established at the time.

## Tensions Between Trump and the Press Continue

The confrontation adds to a broader history of disagreements between Trump and journalists covering his administration.

Trump has repeatedly accused major news organisations of publishing “fake news” and has taken legal action against several media outlets. His critics argue that his frequent attacks on the press risk weakening public confidence in independent journalism. Trump, however, maintains that much of the media coverage he receives is unfair and politically biased.

The latest incident has once again drawn attention to the challenges journalists face when questioning political leaders during official appearances.

Presidential press conferences and public briefings give reporters opportunities to scrutinise government decisions, seek clarification and raise questions on matters of public interest. At the same time, disagreements over the wording and tone of questions can become political controversies in their own right.

The exchange between Trump and Feinberg illustrates the continuing friction between the White House and parts of the American press. Further scrutiny of the incident will depend on the available footage, the full context of the questions asked and the responses from those involved.

articles.title: Sakaja Sacks Mosiria Days After Declaring Nairobi Governorship Bid
articles.summary: The decision comes days after Geoffrey Mosiria declared his intention to challenge Governor Johnson Sakaja in the 2027 General Election, amid reports of disagreements between the two over service delivery and public spending.
articles.body:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has removed Geoffrey Mosiria from his position as Chief Officer for Public Participation, Citizen Engagement and Customer Service, days after Mosiria announced his intention to contest the governorship in the 2027 General Election.

The decision was communicated through a circular dated Wednesday, October 21, 2026, signed by Nairobi County Secretary and Head of Public Service Dr Machel Waikenda. The circular, referenced NCC/CS/003/2026, outlines changes to the responsibilities of senior county officials, with the new arrangements taking effect immediately.

Under the changes, Zipporah Njeri Mwangi will serve as Acting Chief Officer for Public Participation, Citizen Engagement and Customer Service while retaining her existing responsibilities in the City Culture, Arts and Tourism docket. Eng. Samwel Njogu has been appointed Acting Chief Officer for Mobility, while Godfrey Akumali has also been assigned new responsibilities.

The circular cites Sections 44(3)(a), 45(5) and 64 of the County Governments Act, 2012, as the legal basis for the administrative changes. However, it does not provide reasons for Mosiria's removal or indicate whether he has been assigned another role within the county government.

The development comes ten days after Mosiria publicly announced his intention to challenge Sakaja for the Nairobi governorship in the 2027 General Election.

Mosiria made the announcement on October 11 while addressing worshippers at Jesus Is Alive Ministries during a service hosted by Bishop Margaret Wanjiru. He cited his experience in health, environmental management and citizen engagement as preparation for the county's top position, pledging to address challenges affecting service delivery in Nairobi.

His declaration followed reports of disagreements with the governor over the management of county affairs. In an interview on October 19, Mosiria said he had been sidelined following differences over the use of public funds and the delivery of services.

He also indicated that he intended to remain in his county government position until the official campaign period began.

On Wednesday, Mosiria made further allegations on social media, claiming that Sakaja and Embakasi East MP Babu Owino were working together against him. He described himself as their “common enemy.”

Neither Nairobi City Hall nor representatives of Owino had responded to the claims by the time of reporting.

Mosiria also said he was aware of previous legal attempts to challenge his position and vowed to defend himself against allegations he considers false and malicious.

Mosiria has served in several senior positions within the Nairobi County Government since Sakaja took office following the 2022 General Election. He was initially appointed Chief Officer for Health before moving to the Environment docket, where he became known for leading enforcement operations targeting illegal dumping and other environmental violations.

In November 2025, he was transferred to the Public Participation, Citizen Engagement and Customer Service docket as part of an earlier administrative reshuffle.

His removal marks another change in the county government's senior management as political activity gradually intensifies ahead of the 2027 elections.

Mosiria has not announced whether he intends to challenge the decision in court. He has, however, maintained that his ambition to contest the Nairobi governorship remains unchanged.

The circumstances surrounding his removal, including whether the county government will issue a further explanation and whether Mosiria will pursue legal action, remain key issues to watch as the political contest for Nairobi's top seat develops.

articles.title: Meet The Namuyomba Foundation
articles.summary: In a short video on the Namuyomba Comedy Foundation’s Facebook page, a young girl looks straight into the camera and says something simple and sure: she loves entertainment, and one day she wants to be a journalist.
articles.body:
Her name is Mirembe Maria, and she lives at the foundation in Uganda’s Mukono district. The foundation says it has been operating for eight years, using dance, song and drama to support children facing hardship. It also appeals to well-wishers to help cover their basic needs and school costs.

Maria’s list of loves is easy to follow: playing, singing, dancing and reciting. Learning is on it too, and she names it as one of the things she enjoys most. Her interest in the news is not just talk. In several skits on the foundation’s page, she plays a news anchor, copying the presenters she watches on television, with the poise of someone who has studied them closely.

The foundation has noticed. It calls her its “young journalist.”

The group is active well beyond the screen. A post dated 5 July shows it appearing at Comedy Festival 2026 at Uma grounds.

Maria closes her video with a question for everyone watching: “What was your dream when you were my age?” Then she thanks the people who support the foundation.

That support is what the foundation hopes to grow. It wants more people to join its work so that the children in its care can have an education and their basic needs met.

articles.title: A Quarantined Relative Becomes Kenya’s Second Ebola Patient
articles.summary: Kenya confirmed its second Ebola case on October 14: a 39-year-old man who fell ill on October 13 while in quarantine after the first patient, his relative, died on October 5.
articles.body:
Kenya’s health authorities got the warning they were hoping not to need on Wednesday. A man held in mandatory isolation after a relative’s death from Ebola has himself tested positive, bringing the country’s confirmed total to two cases and one death.

The chain of events began with a Kenyan who made his way home from the Democratic Republic of Congo by way of Uganda. He had taken ill in Congo roughly a month earlier, and by the time he reached a Nairobi hospital the disease was far advanced. He died there on October 5.

His family was placed under a 21-day quarantine. On October 13, one member of that household, a 39-year-old man, developed fever, exhaustion and aching joints. Two laboratories, the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the KEMRI-CDC facility, ran their own tests and reached the same result. The pathogen is Bundibugyo, an uncommon species of the Ebola virus.

Health Director General Patrick Amoth announced the findings, and officials were keen to frame them as evidence that the system worked. Because the patient was already being watched, there was no gap between falling ill and being identified, and care could begin at once. The ministry says nothing points to the virus spreading through the wider community. A suspected infection in Wajir, which had briefly drawn attention, came back negative.

How many people the first patient exposed remains unclear. Published figures vary widely: 128 contacts in one account, 57 identified and 10 quarantined in earlier reporting, and 66 in quarantine in a headline. Tracing is an ongoing process, so the totals have likely climbed since the earliest counts. The ministry’s next briefing is the safer source.

The case also places Kenya on a growing list. It is the fourth country to report an infection tied to the Congolese epidemic, now the second-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded, with more than 8,000 cases and upwards of 4,000 deaths. That a sick traveller could cross multiple borders and reach the capital has sharpened scrutiny of screening along the region’s frontiers.

Advice on what to do next pulls in different directions. The World Health Organization wants targeted screening rather than sweeping travel bans, while Amnesty International has asked that the response not trample on rights or turn into excessive surveillance.

The coming days will test whether the quarantine that exposed this case can also contain it. That depends on whether contact tracing keeps pace, and on whether the government can protect public health without eroding civil liberties.

articles.title: A Fight That Never Ends
articles.summary: Kenya’s election is in August 2027, and the contest between President William Ruto and Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has been running for much of this year. Each time one of them speaks, the other answers within a day or two. This week was another round.
articles.body:
Round One: A Man Pushed Out

The fight began as a party quarrel before it became a national one. In February, the ODM National Executive Committee removed Sifuna as Secretary General, and the announcement was made in Mombasa by party leader Oburu Odinga. The party cited discipline and leadership conduct. Sifuna refused to accept it. He said he remained the duly elected Secretary General, vowed to go to court, and claimed his removal followed his firm stance against supporting Ruto’s 2027 reelection.

Whatever the real reason, the ouster changed who Sifuna was to the public. He was no longer a party official defending a line. He had become a man who said he was punished for refusing to back the president, and that gave him a story to tell.

Round Two: The President Responds

Out of the dispute grew Linda Mwananchi. It began with ODM rebels and then drew in leaders from other parties, filling rally grounds in Kisumu, Kisii and across Western Kenya. According to your notes, Ruto responded directly to Sifuna for the first time in July, shortly before a TIFA poll named Sifuna the strongest opposition candidate. That poll put Ruto at 24% and Sifuna at 15%.

From there the attacks went both ways. Ruto claimed that former President Uhuru Kenyatta was funding Linda Mwananchi. Sifuna told him to produce evidence. He said the president had apparently read the claim in a newspaper, and that the movement’s real agenda was to make Ruto a one-term president. No evidence for the funding claim has appeared in the reports I found.

Round Three: The Levy

Sifuna’s next move was on money. He said that if elected he would scrap the affordable housing levy, and he claimed he pays Ksh 24,000 a month in it. At rallies, he called the housing programme a source of white elephants, with cement and steel contracts going to a few people rather than ordinary Kenyans.

On Tuesday in Marakwet East, Ruto answered. He said scrapping the levy would put thousands of jobs at risk and dash the hopes of slum dwellers who want to own homes. He also told residents to register as voters, saying enlistment was low.

Round Four: The Concert

Then came the insult. Sifuna had attended Koffi Olomide’s performance at Fred Obachi Machoka’s 50th media anniversary concert. Ruto mocked the appearance. He said Sifuna and his party had nothing substantive to offer, that all that was left was alcohol, and that asking Kenyans to vote for that insulted their intelligence. In Tiaty, he asked residents to spare him the embarrassment of low voter turnout.

Round Five: The Payslip

Sifuna replied today. He asked whether Ruto was “done ranting” about the 24K, then turned his own payslip into an argument: Ksh 43,000 a month for SHA and Ksh 500,000 in PAYE. He promised that in 2027 they would cut the fat from the budget to bring relief to workers, and he accused the government of spending taxpayers’ money on tea and mandazi at State House.

The pattern is clear. Ruto goes after Sifuna’s character and his housing promise. Sifuna goes after the cost of living and the government’s spending. Neither answers the other’s central point, so each attack leads to another reply.

Why It Keeps Going

The fight continues because each man needs it.

For Ruto, a rival defined as unserious is easier to defeat, and attacking the opposition helps him shift attention from the levies to the opposition’s promises. His call for voter registration suggests he also worries about turnout.
For Sifuna, every attack from the president makes him look like the main challenger. He has said repeatedly that Linda Mwananchi will not split the opposition vote, and his meetings with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka and former Chief Justice David Maraga’s joining the group show he is trying to build a single united ticket.

The harder question for Sifuna is not Ruto. It is whether the opposition will pick him. Rigathi Gachagua says his own supporters want him as candidate, the Luhya Council of Elders has endorsed Sifuna without that becoming a formal nomination, and some in the opposition picture him as a running mate rather than the candidate. Until that is settled, Ruto may be fighting a rival who is not yet the opposition’s choice.

The Fight Ahead

Ten months remain before the vote. The next rounds are easy to predict: more rallies, more claims about taxes and levies, and more replies within a day. The fight will probably end on August 2027, at the ballot box, and not before.

articles.title: Meet “Yesu wa Bombolulu”
articles.summary: A man who has fed congregants, chased people out of church and was headed to hospital on a mission to heal the sick when he was allegedly arrested.
articles.body:
A man known on social media as “Yesu wa Bombolulu”, meaning “Jesus of Bombolulu”, has allegedly been arrested in Mombasa after videos showed him leading a crowd through the streets. The clips have drawn curiosity and mixed reactions from Kenyans online.

According to accounts circulating online, the man has fed congregants at gatherings and has also chased people out of church. On the day he was allegedly arrested, he was reportedly on his way to a hospital on what he described as a mission to heal the sick. However, his real name, age and church affiliation, if any, have not been made public in the reports seen so far.

Meanwhile, the videos of the incident have spread across TikTok and Threads. Some viewers found the scenes amusing, while others voiced concern. Some commenters even suggested that local content creators were having fun with residents, although that claim has not been verified.

He is not the first self-styled messiah to attract police attention in Kenya. In May 2023, Eliud Wekesa, popularly known as “Yesu wa Tongaren”, was arrested during a state crackdown on church activities. A court in Bungoma later ordered a mental assessment and allowed police to hold him for four more days to complete investigations.

For now, many questions remain unanswered. A police statement confirming the arrest had not been found at the time of writing, and it is unclear where the man is being held, whether he has been charged, or what the reason for the arrest was.

This story will be updated as more details emerge.

articles.title: Ruto Promises Roads, Power and a Higher Milk Price in Elgeyo Marakwet
articles.summary: At the rally, the President announced KMTC student hostels, Sh21 billion for roads, electricity for more than 10,000 households and a milk price of Sh65 per litre under new KCC management. He also promoted the Tertiary Placement and Funding Bill, 2026, which would merge three higher education funding bodies, and closed with a call against tribal politics ahead of 2027.
articles.body:
Elgeyo Marakwet County | Tuesday, 13 October 2026

President William Ruto used a rally in Elgeyo Marakwet County today to set out what his government has built and what it plans to deliver. He announced new KMTC student hostels, billions of shillings for roads, electricity for more than 10,000 households and a higher price for milk. He then turned to ethnic politics ahead of the 2027 General Election.

On infrastructure, the President said his government is building KMTC student hostels in the region, and he spoke of a 220-kilometre road project. He also touted the roads his administration has built across the country and said Sh21 billion has been allocated for roads in Elgeyo Marakwet. He addressed matters concerning contractors working on road projects as well. Many of these promises, however, are not new. In January 2025, Ruto announced a 200-bed hostel for the Kerio Valley KMTC campus. In December 2025, Deputy President Kithure Kindiki blamed stalled roads in the county on non-payment of contractors and promised that the Kapyego-Chesoi and Chesoi-Tirap-Embobut roads would be completed.

Power was another major theme. Ruto said the government will connect more than 10,000 houses to electricity under its last-mile connectivity programme. This also builds on an earlier pledge, since Kindiki had said Sh780 million was set aside to connect more than 9,000 homes in the county.

Turning to farmers, the President said new management at New KCC will raise the price paid for milk to Sh65 per litre. He has been raising that figure in recent weeks. Earlier this month, he said the price was Sh50 and heading to Sh60, and that the government would clear Sh8 billion owed by the processor. Even so, the sector faces pressure. Farmers and consumers have complained of shortages and rising prices, and figures cited in reports show that formal milk deliveries to processors fell from 84.4 million litres in June to 81.3 million litres in July.

Ruto also addressed higher education, speaking about the Tertiary Placement and Funding Bill, 2026. The bill would merge the Higher Education Loans Board, the Universities Fund and the TVET Funding Board into a single authority. The President has said every student placed in a public university or college will receive full funding. However, reports say the proposed model leans heavily on student loans.

He ended with a message on ethnic politics. Ruto has said before that he will not allow tribal politics to thrive in Kenya, and on Monday in Nandi he told residents that Kenya will vote as one people in 2027.

Today’s rally is part of an 11-day tour of six North Rift counties, with roads, housing, markets, hospitals and electricity featuring prominently on his itinerary. The schedule for the day included breaking ground for Kerio Valley KMTC student hostels, a water project and a market, and commissioning the Kipkuldul-Kapyego-Kamalei road. Nevertheless, the opposition has criticised the tour as a campaign for 2027, and with the election still about a year away, the President’s promises will be closely watched.

articles.title: Mosiria Enters Nairobi Governor Race, Vows to “Fix” the City
articles.summary: Nairobi County Chief Officer Geoffrey Mosiria has declared his bid for the Nairobi governorship in the 2027 General Election. He is presenting himself as “Mr Fix-it” and promising to improve service delivery in the capital.
articles.body:
On Sunday, October 11, Geoffrey Mosiria stood in a church hosted by Bishop Margaret Wanjiru and declared that he wants to be Nairobi’s next governor. It was an awkward announcement, because he currently works for the man he wants to unseat. Mosiria is the county’s Chief Officer for Citizen Engagement and Customer Service, and Governor Johnson Sakaja is his boss.He had floated the idea ten days earlier, on October 1, saying former governor Mike Sonko had advised him to aim for the top seat. He has also said he is seeking a meeting with Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i in the hope of an endorsement. His pitch is “Mr Fix-it”: one term, he says, is enough to fix Nairobi. He also says Sakaja tried to dim his rising star. His path to this point has been a busy one, moving from health to environment in August 2024 and then to citizen engagement.

The campaign trail

The Wanjiru connection may complicate things. Mosiria floated the bishop as a possible running mate, but Matiang’i has since backed her for governor, and she says she will not withdraw.

A record built on crackdowns

Mosiria’s public profile rests on enforcement. In 2025 he announced rules switching off matatu music in the CBD, along with night-time noise measurements that led to equipment being seized the next morning. He went after churches in Pipeline and clubs in Kilimani, and some clubs went to court to block enforcement.

He has also led inspections of waste disposal by CBD hotels and businesses, and more recently urged building owners to repaint and light up their properties.

His record on street people is mixed. In June 2025 he said he took a woman with two children home to Kakamega, with well-wishers helping with shopping. Around the same time, he called for a crackdown on people who use children to exploit public sympathy. Critics may point to that contrast.

His methods have drawn pushback. Mpasho headlines mention an outcry in August 2026 over jaywalkers being made to clean streets without gloves, and a KSh10 million lawsuit by Oga Obinna, though I only have the headlines, not the details.

The Babu Owino feud

The campaign is also colliding with an old rivalry. In a September post, Mosiria said his dispute with Embakasi East MP Babu Owino goes back to student politics at the University of Nairobi (SONU). He claims goons sent by Babu attacked him at the Kikuyu and Upper Kabete campuses and demanded money, adding that he has forgiven but not forgotten. Earlier this year, he called Babu an extortionist and said he would expose him. I found no response from Babu to the campus allegations.

The two have clashed over current politics too. On September 25, Mosiria disputed Babu’s claim that his party registered 660,008 members in six days, saying the real figure was about 46,000. Babu, who has declared himself the frontrunner for governor, has criticised the hawker evictions as harassment of the urban poor. Mosiria replied that Babu was weaponising poverty.

The attacks have gone both ways. An old video resurfaced of Babu making claims about why Mosiria left the University of Nairobi, and Mosiria’s lawyer wrote to the university seeking clarification. I found no confirmation either way.

What to watch

Mosiria’s candidacy raises several questions. Can a serving official run against his own boss? Will Matiang’i’s backing of Wanjiru close the door on his hoped-for endorsement? And will a record of high-profile crackdowns draw voters or put them off? With the election still about a year away, he and Babu Owino look set to keep trading blows.

articles.title: Carrick’s Struggling United Head to Madrid Seeking a Lift Against Atlético
articles.summary: Manchester United visit a resurgent Atlético Madrid tonight with their domestic season in difficulty, hoping Europe can offer relief from their worst Premier League start in almost four decades.
articles.body:
Manchester United arrive at the Metropolitano tonight carrying the weight of a troubled league campaign, and in need of something to lift the mood around Michael Carrick’s team. Six points from six Premier League games is their poorest opening since 1986-87, and Saturday’s 1-1 home draw with Tottenham left them winless in four, with boos echoing around Old Trafford at full time. Kick-off in Madrid is at 10:00 pm East Africa Time, 8:00 pm in the UK.

Their form in the Champions League has been far more encouraging. A 4-0 victory over Sabah in the opening round of the new 36-team league phase has put United fourth in the standings with three points. At home, the picture is bleaker. One win in six has left them 13th, 12 points behind leaders Manchester City, and their results read a defeat at Hull, a 5-2 win at Ipswich, a 2-2 draw with Everton, a loss to City, and draws with Fulham and Tottenham.

Atlético, meanwhile, offer a study in contrast. They sit 25th in the European table with no points after a 2-1 defeat at Liverpool, yet in La Liga they have won four in a row, a run that includes a 2-1 derby victory over Real Madrid and another by the same score at Alavés on Saturday. Their 19 points leave them second, behind Barcelona, who have won all eight of their games.

United will also be wary of the history between the clubs. They have never beaten Atlético in a competitive fixture, and the sides last met in the 2021-22 Champions League last 16. The first leg in Madrid ended 1-1, and Atlético progressed after winning 1-0 at Old Trafford.

Team news favours the hosts. Atlético are expected to have a full squad, with no injuries or suspensions reported. United are without five players by one account, though other outlets count six. Matthijs de Ligt has returned to the travelling party, and young defender Dan Armer is also in the group. Predicted line-ups suggest Manchester United will line up in a 4-2-3-1 with Lammens in goal, Dalot, Martínez, Maguire and Yoro in defence, Santos and Tielemans in midfield, and Rashford, Fernandes and Mbeumo behind Cunha. Atlético are tipped to play a 4-4-2 built around Oblak, with Pubill, Romero, Hancko and Grimaldo in front of him, a midfield of G. Simeone, Barrios, Koke and Baena, and Álvarez partnering Kang-in Lee up front. These are only forecasts, with confirmed teams usually released about an hour before kick-off, and some outlets expect Carrick to make changes.

Diego Simeone, for his part, has refused to treat United’s slump as a reason for comfort. He has warned his players that the visitors are a very aggressive side capable of making things difficult, and reminded them that this is still Manchester United.

The statistical models lean towards the Spanish side, giving Atlético a 49 per cent chance of victory, against 26 per cent for United and 25 per cent for a draw. The stakes differ for each club. A result in Madrid would ease a difficult week for United, while a win would lift Atlético out of the bottom half of the table after their loss at Anfield.

Attention will turn quickly to the weekend. Atlético travel to Espanyol on Saturday, then to Stuttgart in the Champions League on 20 October. United go to Leeds on Sunday, with kick-off at 4:00 pm East Africa Time, before an away European tie at Como on 21 October.

articles.title: “I Was Offered Running Mate Slot”: Methu Claims Goverment Camp Plot to Split Opposition
articles.summary: Nyandarua Senator John Methu claims government-linked individuals offered to fund a party and rallies for him, attack him in public while backing him in private, and later make him President William Ruto’s 2027 running mate. He says Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro advised him to reject the plan, promised to join the DCP, and then formed his own party. Methu says Nyoro can be named a “mole.” The claims are unverified, and Nyoro and State House had not responded at the time of publishing.
articles.body:
NAIROBI: Nyandarua Senator John Methu has made explosive claims of a plot to split the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election. He alleges that people linked to the government offered to bankroll a political party for him, and he has turned on a close ally who he says promised to join the opposition.

Speaking on Citizen TV on Sunday, Methu said individuals from the government approached him with a proposal to form a political party. He said they would finance the party and its rallies in private while publicly appearing to oppose him. According to Methu, the two sides would later converge, and he would be named President William Ruto’s running mate.

The senator said he rejected the offer and called Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro, whom he regards as a friend, to tell him about it. Methu said Nyoro advised him not to fall for the trap, warning that a new party would divide the united opposition. He said Nyoro also told him he would soon join the Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) and be part of the opposition.

Methu said that is not what happened. To his surprise, Nyoro formed his own political party, which he said contradicted their discussions and agreements. “If I was to name moles, then I think the name Ndindi Nyoro will feature prominently,” Methu said.

The claims come as Mount Kenya’s politics shifts ahead of next year’s polls. Nyoro, once a close Ruto ally, has become a vocal critic of the government and is the subject of speculation about presidential ambitions.

Methu did not name the officials who approached him and offered no evidence for the alleged offer. Nyoro and State House had not responded to the claims at the time of publishing.

articles.title: ICT Authority Opens Web Design Training for 40 Professionals and Students
articles.summary: NAIROBI: The ICT Authority is offering a 16-day virtual course in web design and development, part of a government push to build digital skills among Kenyans.
articles.body:
The training, run with CAP Youth Empowerment Institute Kenya, will take place from October 21 to November 5, 2026. Sessions run from 5:30 p.m. to 8:00 p.m., an evening slot meant to suit working professionals and students who cannot attend during the day. It is part of the Citizens Digital Skills Programme, under the national Training 20 Million Citizens initiative.

Participants will get hands-on practice with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, the core tools behind most websites. The organizers say the aim is for graduates to build responsive, real-world websites that work across phones, tablets and desktop computers. Trainees will also join the Smart Academy tech community, which could help them find collaborators, mentors and job leads after the course ends.

The timing reflects growing demand for web skills in Kenya’s economy. Small businesses, schools and service providers increasingly need an online presence to reach customers, and many cannot afford large agency fees. For students and young professionals, a short practical course can be a low-cost way to turn a skill into freelance income or a stronger job application.

Space is limited to 40 slots. The ICT Authority says registration closes on October 20, 2026, though a promotional poster for the same course gives October 18, so applicants should register early. Interested applicants should register through the official Smart Academy portal at smartacademy.go.ke, and find further information on the ICT Authority website at icta.go.ke. The ICT Authority says questions can go to capacity.dev@ict.go.ke or citizens@icta.go.ke. The announcement does not state whether the training carries a fee, and Smart Academy’s course catalog lists its standard web design course at Ksh 5,000, so applicants should confirm the cost with the organizers before registering.

articles.title: Ex-KDF Soldier Patrick Osoi Eyes State House After Terror Charges, Bail and a Viral Movement
articles.summary: NAIROBI: Patrick Osoi, the former soldier who shot to national attention last year after launching the Fighting Brutality and Impunity (FBI) movement, now says he wants to be Kenya’s president in 2027.
articles.body:
Osoi told The Kenya Times he is ready to lead the country and that his first order of business would be to confront corruption. He has also encouraged young Kenyans to go for elective seats and back one another at the ballot. His X account already calls him the 6th President of the Republic of Kenya. No party affiliation or formal candidacy has been reported, so he remains an aspirant for now.

From charcoal seller to the political stage

According to profiles, Osoi was born in Vihiga County in 1990 and grew up in Embu County. He reportedly sold charcoal and books as a young man. He went to Siakago Boys High School and later studied automotive engineering at the National Youth Service School of Engineering. He then earned a degree in Logistics Management from Moi University.

By his own account, he served as a KDF Special Forces soldier and an NIS officer, and later in the US Army. One profile says he was a senior business intelligence analyst and ground forces commander between 2014 and 2020. It adds that he served as an air-assault specialist and armorer in the US Army during the COVID-19 period. Those claims come largely from Osoi and the profiles built on his account, and they haven’t been independently confirmed.

After leaving service, he reportedly founded Capital Choice Investments Ltd, a company said to have interests in real estate, healthcare and media in Kenya and the United States.

The movement that made him famous

Osoi’s public profile rose sharply on July 28, 2025, when he announced the FBI movement. He said he had formed it with ex-officers Jackson Kuria Kimani, popularly known as Cop Shakur, and Kimathi Hiram. The group said it would stand with Kenyans abused by police who follow illegal orders. It named the victims of the June 25, 2024 protests, families of those killed, and officers it said had been abandoned by the system. His post drew more than 260,000 views on X.

Arrest, charges and bail

Police arrested him the next day. His team described it as an abduction by heavily armed men. At Kahawa Law Courts, prosecutors told the court he faced charges including intent to commit a felony, firearm and ammunition possession, and offences linked to terrorism recruitment and facilitation. They said he was planning attacks on police officers around the June 25 and Saba Saba protests.

Osoi and his colleagues rejected the claims. They described the movement as a peaceful civic platform pushing for justice, accountability and constitutionalism, and called for the Terrorism Act to be reviewed. These remain allegations, and they were contested in court.

On August 8, 2025, a magistrate released Osoi and Cop Shakur on Sh50,000 cash bail or a Sh200,000 bond with a surety of the same amount. Their defense was led by Embakasi East MP Babu Owino.

articles.title: Ruto’s Buffalo Plan Is Old News: Kenya Has Been Planning This Since 2018
articles.summary: Buffalo Farming Is Not a New Idea: Kenya Has Had the Policy for Years, and Only Delivery Is Missing
articles.body:
When President William Ruto floated the idea of milking buffaloes to ease Kenya’s dairy shortage, many Kenyans heard it as a surprise. It isn’t one. The plan has been sitting in government files for years, and what has been missing all along is the follow-through.

Speaking at the Agriculture and Food Systems Transformation Summit in Nairobi, the president pointed to India, where buffaloes are a pillar of the dairy trade. “If others are milking them, why can’t we do the same?” he asked, arguing that the country needs more sources of milk. He said he has asked the Livestock Development PS, Jonathan Mueke, to help find better camel breeds and buffaloes, and suggested starting small.

The paper trail shows how old the idea is. Farmers began asking the Ministry of Agriculture about keeping the animals as far back as 2018. Kenya and Brazil have since endorsed a protocol covering the trade in them, with the Kenya Animal Genetic Resources Centre (KAGRC) and farmers who applied set to hold the first stock. Then, on January 31, 2025, Agriculture CS Mutahi Kagwe signed a gazette notice declaring the domesticated water buffalo a food animal under the Meat Control Act. A two-year pilot was outlined, limited to KAGRC and approved farmers.

So the legal door has been open for well over a year. Yet reports at the time noted that the species was not in the country, and critics asked where the animals would come from and how they would be brought in. Whether any have arrived since is not clear from the public record.

The practical hurdles are real. Buffaloes would need health checks, disease monitoring, enough feed and water, and breeding know-how. Government would also have to work out import costs and expected milk output, and whether processors will buy it. Conservationists add that the animal in question is the domestic water buffalo, a different species from the wild Cape buffalo seen in Kenya’s parks.

For Kenyans the message is simple: the policy exists, the president is now publicly pushing it, and the test will be whether animals actually reach farms.

articles.title: Ronaldo Shown the Touchline by Portugal While Officials Weigh His Fate
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo is out of Portugal’s plans for now. The country’s football governing body has sidelined its all-time leading scorer while it investigates why he abandoned the squad earlier this month.
articles.body:
For the first time in a long career, Portugal’s most celebrated player finds himself on the wrong side of his own federation. Cristiano Ronaldo has been told to stay away from national duty until administrators decide how to treat his sudden exit from the squad’s base in Copenhagen.

The trouble began on September 30, when the veteran forward packed up and left after a falling-out with coach Jorge Jesus over how the team was being run. Nine days later, the federation’s disciplinary arm stepped in, and by Saturday it had made its stance public: Ronaldo would sit out while the matter is examined, and the file was flagged as pressing.

Fans hoping for answers soon will have to wait. Those handling the case have chosen silence for now, promising no updates until their inquiry wraps up and naming no date for a conclusion. They were also keen to point out that sitting him out is a holding measure, not a verdict, and that nothing has yet been proven against him.

What he could face is written into the federation’s own rules. Players who stay away from team commitments without a good reason risk a ban lasting anywhere from a month to half a year, along with a modest fine of between €500 and €1,000. Ronaldo’s clean disciplinary history and two decades in the national shirt may count in his favour, though his role as captain could just as easily be held against him.

The player himself has taken a notably humble line. He has said sorry to his teammates and supporters, accepted that his actions deserve a response, and insisted he wants to return once the matter is settled.

The calendar adds urgency. Should officials choose a ban beyond a month, Portugal would line up against Denmark and Wales without their talisman. Until a decision arrives, the question hanging over the squad is simple: a short break from the team, or a long one?

articles.title: Old Trafford showdown: Man United and Tottenham seek a lift tonight
articles.summary: Two struggling sides meet in Manchester this evening. Here is how they are expected to line up and who is unavailable.
articles.body:
Neither Manchester United nor Tottenham has had the start to the season it wanted, and tonight at Old Trafford one of them gets a chance to change that. Kickoff is at 7:30 PM East Africa Time.

United sit 12th on five points and are chasing only their second league win of the campaign under Michael Carrick. Their visitors are in a deeper hole. Spurs are bottom of the table with two points and still waiting for a first victory. History also favours the visitors: United have beaten them just once in their last nine meetings, a 2-0 win at home in February.

The official team sheets should arrive roughly an hour before kickoff. Until then, here is how the teams are expected to look.

United are tipped to play 4-2-3-1. Senne Lammens is expected in goal, behind a back four of Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw, the same group that has started recently. Carlos Baleba, the summer signing, is expected to anchor midfield next to Youri Tielemans, although some previews give Kobbie Mainoo that role. Captain Bruno Fernandes should play behind Matheus Cunha, with Bryan Mbeumo wide on one side and Marcus Rashford, if fit, on the other.

Rashford is not certain to play. He, Mainoo and Amad Diallo have only trained lightly after the international break, and Matthijs de Ligt is also in doubt. Carrick has confirmed that Patrick Dorgu will be out for several weeks with a hamstring problem picked up on international duty. Benjamin Sesko, Manuel Ugarte and several other players are sidelined, and Noussair Mazraoui is a doubt after a knock with Morocco.

Tottenham, who are also expected to line up in a 4-2-3-1, have a few decisions left. Previews disagree on the back line and midfield, with Antonin Kinsky tipped in goal, Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke available in defence, and Sandro Tonali in midfield. Up front, Dominic Solanke is expected to lead the line with Omar Marmoush and Savinho on the flanks. Roberto De Zerbi has said van de Ven and van Hecke are fit, though he is mindful of the personal side for van Hecke, whose twins were born this week. Dejan Kulusevski has trained but is unlikely to start.

articles.title: Changing your number? What Kenya’s plan for recycled lines means for you
articles.summary: The Communications Authority wants a shared record of phone numbers that have passed to new owners. Here is how it could affect your line, your M-Pesa and your bank alerts.
articles.body:
The Communications Authority wants a shared record of phone numbers that have passed to new owners. Here is how it could affect your line, your M-Pesa and your bank alerts.
Story
Ever received a text meant for a stranger, such as a bank alert or a one-time code? The Communications Authority of Kenya (CA) says it is working on a way to stop that happening.
The regulator intends to build a single national record of mobile numbers that have been given to new users. Banks, fintech companies and other businesses that message customers would check it before sending, so their texts don’t land with the wrong person. Mobile operators such as Safaricom and Airtel would update the record every three months with the lines they have switched off or handed on. The CA has pointed to a similar system run in the United States as its model.
The database sits inside a bigger set of rules about what happens to lines that go unused. Under the draft, an operator must publish the numbers it is about to switch off at least 30 days beforehand, including in a newspaper sold across the country. Companies would also have to get a customer’s clear approval, through a business-specific USSD request, before sending them commercial messages. And before an operator gives a used number to someone new, it must wipe the old owner’s personal details and linked services from that line.
For many people, the real worry is being locked out. If you leave an old number idle and it is later reassigned, you could lose access to services tied to it, including mobile money.
The CA says there are safeguards. Operators must announce which numbers are due to be switched off and offer a USSD service where you can check whether yours is affected. Anyone who expects to be out of reach for more than six months, because of illness or time in prison for example, can ask to have their number protected.
Pressure for clearer rules has come from several directions. A prisoner who lost his number while in custody took the issue to court in June 2024, and Members of Parliament have asked Safaricom how it handles the lines of customers who stop using their SIM cards.
The database itself is not live. The CA’s updated rules came into force on September 19, but the parts that depend on the database will only apply once it has been built.
In the meantime, you can protect yourself by keeping important lines active with an occasional call or small top-up, updating your number with your bank and other accounts if you switch, and letting your operator know in advance if you will be unreachable for a long time.

articles.title: Ministry of Health Issues Ebola Prevention Guidance After Kenya Confirms First Imported Case
articles.summary: The Ministry of Health has confirmed Kenya’s first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease and issued guidance on how to prevent infection. Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale says Kenya is not experiencing an outbreak. He urges the public to stay vigilant without panic and to rely on official information. Anyone with questions can call the toll-free 719 line.
articles.body:
NAIROBI, Kenya, October 8, 2026: The Ministry of Health has issued public guidance on preventing Ebola after confirming Kenya’s first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease.

The patient was a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Africa CDC says the patient travelled by road from the DRC to Uganda, spent a night there, then flew to Kenya. The patient was quickly identified, isolated and tested, and died on October 6.

Speaking during a tour of Nairobi Hospital’s 133-bed Ebola Isolation Unit, Cabinet Secretary Duale reassured Kenyans that the country is not experiencing an Ebola outbreak. He said the confirmed case was imported.

How to protect yourself

The Ministry advises the public to:

Wash hands frequently with soap and water, or use an alcohol-based hand rub.
Avoid close contact with sick people arriving from countries reporting active Ebola transmission.
Seek care promptly at a recognised health facility if you feel unwell.
Report anyone who is unwell to the nearest health facility.
Be honest on health declaration forms if you are travelling, to support surveillance and contact tracing.

The Ministry urges Kenyans to stay vigilant without panic and to follow official Ministry of Health channels for updates. The toll-free 719 health information line is open to anyone seeking guidance.

Contact tracing under way

The Ministry first reported 28 contacts, including family members and health workers who attended to the patient. Its latest update puts the number at 57. Ten have been accounted for and placed under quarantine at the National Police Service Hospital in Nairobi, while tracing of the rest continues.

Kenya’s preparedness

Kenya has been on high alert since May 2026, when outbreaks were declared in the DRC and Uganda. According to the Ministry and WHO:

4,971 health workers have been trained in Ebola prevention and case management.
Over 652,000 travellers have been screened at entry points, and 267 suspected samples have been tested.
Kenya has 15 isolation and treatment units, with plans to expand to 22, prioritising high-risk counties.

Health workers have been urged to apply infection prevention and control measures consistently. Africa CDC is sending a high-level team to Kenya to support the response and has called for stronger surveillance and cross-border information sharing across the region.

articles.title: HELB Clears Five Tuition Batches as Students Await Upkeep Funds
articles.summary: On October 8, 2026, HELB announced it has paid tuition funds for batches HELB-007139, 007145, 007147, 007146 and 007132 directly to institutions. Students whose batches aren’t listed should keep checking their portals, as this doesn’t mean their applications failed.
articles.body:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Thursday, October 8, 2026: The Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) has confirmed that it has disbursed five batches of tuition funds to universities and colleges. The announcement follows weeks of frustration from students who say their loans have been stuck at the allocation stage.

In a statement, HELB said batches HELB-007139, 007145, 007147, 007146 and 007132 have been processed and paid to institutions. The money covers tuition only and goes straight to schools, not to students.

For many students, the bigger worry is upkeep. Those who have not yet received it are likely to wait longer, as the board is still processing payments. HELB says disbursement has begun and it will contact affected students once funds reach their accounts. It has not given a date.

Frustration online

The delay has drawn sharp complaints on social media. Some students say their universities have already confirmed their enrolment, yet no upkeep has arrived. One applicant said disbursement had been “in process” for about three weeks.

HELB officials have said allocation is complete but that actual payment depends on the timely release of government funds, a problem that has recurred over several academic years.

A schedule built on batches

HELB has not published a calendar with fixed payment dates. Funds are released in phases using batch numbers, so a student’s “Approved with Batch Number” status in the portal effectively shows where they sit in the queue. Third-party estimates suggest four to eight weeks from approval to payment, with tuition usually moving faster than upkeep. That is not an official HELB timeline.

Students whose batch numbers were not among the five paid are advised to keep checking their portals and official HELB communication rather than assume their applications have failed.

What students should do
Check your status: Log into the HELB student portal or dial *642#.
Wait for the SurePay message: Students receiving upkeep through M-Pesa should wait for the SurePay confirmation message before trying to withdraw. After the second confirmation message, funds can be accessed through *642#.
Confirm with your institution: Check that your university has completed its confirmation process.
Contact HELB: Call the contact centre on 0711 052 000 or email contactcentre@helb.co.ke. The centre opens from 8:00am to 5:00pm, though this listing dates from February 2026, so confirm it on helb.co.ke.
Offices open, but no need to queue

HELB staff and board directors recently joined students, loanees and parents at the HELB offices in Nairobi to mark Customer Service Week 2026, gathering feedback on service delivery. The board has also reminded students that they no longer need to visit its offices to find out where their loans stand, since status can be checked online or by phone.

For now, students are left waiting for the next batch announcement.

articles.title: Harambee Starlets Run Riot, Thrash Seychelles 11-0 in Olympic Qualifier

articles.body:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Thursday, October 8, 2026: Kenya’s Harambee Starlets opened their road to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games in emphatic style, demolishing Seychelles 11-0 in the first leg of their second-round CAF qualifier at the Ulinzi Sports Complex.

Valary Nekesa set the tone with the opening goal early in the first half. She added a second just before the break to put Kenya 3-0 up at half-time. Interim head coach Godfrey “Solo” Oduor, newly appointed to the role, made several changes to the side that featured at Wafcon. He recalled forwards Jentrix Shikangwa and Corazone Aquino, and gave opportunities to fresh talent. Several experienced players were left out, and the changes paid off.

articles.title: Wamuchomba Quits UDA, Says She Will Defend Githunguri Seat on Another Ticket
articles.summary: Githunguri MP Gathoni Wamuchomba has left the ruling UDA party, citing ethnic hostility in political speech and what she calls the government's failure to act on it. She says she will seek a third term in 2027 but has not yet named her new party.
articles.body:
Githunguri MP Gathoni Wamuchomba has officially quit the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that she will defend her seat in the 2027 General Election on another party's ticket.

Speaking at a press conference at Parliament Buildings on Thursday, the two-term legislator said her decision followed soul-searching and consultations with voters, community leaders and the church. She said her conscience would no longer let her associate with leaders who show no regard for other communities.

Wamuchomba singled out Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, whose remarks she said targeted the Mount Kenya community. She said she had waited for the government to act, but only some MPs were arrested over statements similar to the Cabinet Secretary's. She accused the administration of double speak and said her calls for disciplinary action had gone unheeded.

"I am not going to align myself with the UDA government," she said, adding that she will neither campaign nor seek any seat through the party.

The exit follows her August 31 threat to withdraw support for President William Ruto if Duale and nominated MP Joseph Wainaina were not arrested over alleged hate speech.

The MP did not say which party she will join. She said she will first consult her constituents, who she says will guide her choice of political vehicle. She was categorical that she is staying in elective politics and will seek a third consecutive term.

Her departure is the latest turn in a rocky relationship with UDA. Elected on its ticket in 2022, she said in February 2025 that she would not vie under the party again, citing unmet promises to farmers, heavy taxation and mandatory payslip deductions. She left the party at the height of the Gen-Z protests, then rejoined in January 2026, telling a State House meeting that she wanted to focus on development. She was once a staunch ally of former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua before the two fell out.

Her move adds to the wave of defections from UDA in the Mount Kenya region as the 2027 race draws closer.

Stay updated at vanywinner.co.ke
