articles.title: Linda Mwananchi Says There Is "Some Light" in Party Rebrand Process
articles.summary: The movement's official Facebook page signals progress as Sifuna's camp works to turn TEP into the Linda Mwananchi Movement.
articles.body:
By Newsroom | 8 October 2026

NAIROBI. The official Linda Mwananchi Facebook page has said there is "some light" in the process of rebranding The Equitable Party (TEP) into the Linda Mwananchi Movement, a sign that the movement sees progress as it works toward the 2027 General Election.

The page did not give further details in the post. It is not yet clear what specific step it was referring to, and neither the Registrar of Political Parties nor the party's top officials had publicly elaborated at the time of publishing.

How the plan came about

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna was unveiled as TEP leader and presidential candidate at a launch in Nairobi on Sunday, 4 October. He said TEP had been made available to the movement as an existing political platform, after earlier efforts to set up a new party for the movement failed to produce the desired result.

At the launch, Sifuna said the party would seek to rebrand as the Linda Mwananchi Movement "in the coming days", in line with a decision by the movement's principals. TEP's National Executive Council has since approved the proposed rebrand.

The name question

The Registrar of Political Parties approved reservation of the Linda Mwananchi Movement name on 1 October, after the Political Parties Disputes Tribunal directed the office to reconsider an earlier rejection. The reservation is reported to last 90 days, during which the movement must move from a reserved name to an actual political organisation.

The name is still contested. Charles Wanyonyi has asked the Registrar to give priority to his application for "Linda Mwananchi, Party of Kenya", saying he applied on 24 February, before the application that led to the reservation.

The clock is ticking

Parties taking part in the 2027 election must submit the names and specimen signatures of their authorised officials by 15 October. That leaves Sifuna's team only days to align its officials and its proposed new identity with the electoral process.

Sifuna has said that if further hurdles block the change, the party will keep the name The Equitable Party. That means his 2027 plans don't depend on the rebrand being completed.

What the movement says it stands for

Sifuna has presented Linda Mwananchi as an alternative platform focused on farmers under economic pressure, jobless young people, small businesses facing taxes, and families struggling with education and healthcare costs. He says he wants politics built around ideas, accountability and service rather than personalities.

For now, the Linda Mwananchi page's message is a sign of optimism rather than confirmation that the rebrand is complete.

articles.title: Free Commuter Train Tickets: Where to Get Them, and How to Avoid Scams
articles.summary: Kenya Railways and KRA have teamed up for Customer Service Week. Here is how to find the official details.
articles.body:
By Newsroom | 8 October 2026

NAIROBI. Kenya Railways has announced free commuter train tickets for members of the public, as part of this year's Customer Service Week celebrations. The corporation said it partnered with the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) on the offer, which it announced on Tuesday, 6 October.

What we know so far

Kenya Railways has not said which routes, dates or how many tickets will be given out, or what conditions apply. Customer Service Week is reported to run from 5 to 9 October 2026, which would mean the offer is short-lived. Kenya Railways has not confirmed the dates, so commuters should check before planning a trip around it.

The corporation has asked interested Kenyans to follow its official social media pages for details on routes, dates and how to get the tickets.

Where to look for the details

Kenya Railways: its verified social media accounts and its website, krc.co.ke
KRA: its official X account, @KRACorporate, and its website, kra.go.ke

Beware of scams

Free tickets are exactly the kind of offer fraudsters use. Kenya Railways has repeatedly warned about fake websites and social media pages that pretend to represent it and take payments from passengers. It has said it does not run an official TikTok account, and it has urged the public to report suspicious pages.

Commuters should keep these points in mind:

Don't pay anyone for a "free" ticket.
Don't share personal or payment details through links sent on WhatsApp or from unknown pages.
Check any announcement against Kenya Railways' own verified channels before acting on it.
Report suspicious pages or individuals to Kenya Railways' customer service.

Booking normal tickets

Outside promotions like this one, Kenya Railways says Madaraka Express tickets should be bought only through its official online booking portal, its USSD code *639#, or at its stations.

A wider push on the rails

The offer comes as Kenya Railways continues to modernise Nairobi's commuter network, including a rail link being developed to serve the Talanta Sports City Stadium ahead of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

For now, the free tickets appear to be a short-term customer appreciation gesture rather than a permanent change to fares.

articles.title: Messi Bids Farewell to Argentina with a Goal, Two Assists and a Win
articles.summary: After 21 years and 208 appearances, football's greatest talisman signs off at the Monumental, and says he is not leaving the game.
articles.body:
By Newsroom | 8 October 2026

BUENOS AIRES. Lionel Messi's international story ended the way Argentina had hoped it would: with a win, a goal and a stadium on its feet.

In front of a sold-out Estadio Monumental on Tuesday, Argentina beat Benin 3-0 in "The Last Tango", Messi's 208th and final appearance for his country.

A night made for Messi

The breakthrough came early in the second half. Messi swung in a corner and Nicolás Otamendi rose to head home in the 48th minute. Thirteen minutes later, Messi slipped a pass through to Nico Paz, who curled in a spectacular second.

Then came the moment the crowd had been waiting for. In the 71st minute, Messi stepped up to a penalty and sent it into the roof of the net, his 126th and last goal for Argentina. The stadium erupted into a chant of "Messi, Messi" that has echoed through Argentine football for two decades.

At the final whistle, Messi was handed the match ball, surrounded by family and fighting back tears.

Why it ended now

Messi announced his international retirement on 31 August in a message on Instagram. He said he had given everything he had and wanted a new generation of players to get their chance. He wrote the message two days after Argentina's 1-0 extra-time loss to Spain in the World Cup final.

The Argentine Football Association then invited him back for the farewell it said he deserved, and Messi accepted. Members of the 2022 World Cup-winning squad and their families joined him for the occasion.

A career in numbers

Messi leaves as Argentina's record appearance-maker and leading scorer, with 126 goals. He is also the national team's all-time assist leader. He scored 21 of his goals at World Cups and played in six of them, a record he shares with Cristiano Ronaldo.

He briefly retired from international football in 2016, then went on to the most successful stretch of his career with Argentina, winning the Copa América in 2021 and 2024, and lifting the World Cup in 2022.

Not the end of football

Messi's retirement is from international football only. He will keep playing for Inter Miami, where his contract runs through the 2028 season.

The next question for Argentina is a symbolic one: who will inherit the number 10 shirt?

articles.title: Speaker Wetang'ula Suspends Ndindi Nyoro for Five Sittings Over KPC Share Claims
articles.summary: National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula has suspended Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro for five sitting days after he refused to withdraw and apologise for claims that calls from higher offices influenced government agencies to buy Kenya Pipeline Company (KPC) shares. The Speaker ruled that the refusal amounted to grossly disorderly conduct under the Standing Orders.
articles.body:
National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula on Wednesday suspended Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro from the House for five sitting days, after the legislator declined to retract and apologise for remarks linking phone calls from higher offices to the purchase of Kenya Pipeline Company (KPC) shares by government agencies.

Wetang'ula ruled that Nyoro's refusal to withdraw the statement amounted to grossly disorderly conduct under the House's Standing Orders.

How it unfolded

The Speaker first challenged Nyoro to substantiate his claim that calls had been made to influence the share purchases, then directed him to apologise. Nyoro declined, insisting that what he had said was the truth and that the truth rides higher than the rules.

Nyoro then asked for two weeks to table evidence. Wetang'ula responded that the remarks had already been struck from the Hansard, leaving nothing to substantiate.

Citing Standing Orders 88, 107 and 107A, which deal with retraction and apology and the consequences of ignoring the Speaker's direction, the Speaker offered Nyoro another chance to apologise. The MP again declined.

Wetang'ula said he was imposing the most lenient punishment available and ordered Nyoro to leave the Chamber while the House continued its business.

Nyoro's reaction

Speaking at a press conference after the ruling, Nyoro said it was unfortunate that he had been suspended for speaking the truth.

He also said that President William Ruto could buy the entire Parliament but would never place any value on some MPs. This is Nyoro's own opinion and was not backed with evidence in the reports.

Background

Recent coverage describes Nyoro as the leader of the People's Party of Kenya, which has joined the united opposition.

This is not his first suspension from the House. In January 2022, he was removed from Parliament for two days for claiming that MPs were being bribed to vote, an allegation he could not substantiate. Earlier, under then-Speaker Justin Muturi, he was suspended for four days over bribery claims relating to the Building Bridges Initiative (BBI) Bill.

articles.title: Pedro Rodríguez Retires from Football at 39
articles.summary: Former Barcelona, Chelsea and Spain winger Pedro Rodríguez has retired after a career that brought a World Cup, a European Championship and three Champions League titles.
articles.body:
Former Barcelona, Chelsea and Spain winger Pedro Rodríguez has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 39.

The Tenerife-born forward shared the news on Wednesday in a message on social media. "I feel the time has come," he wrote, adding that he was ready to begin a new chapter in his life. He said he leaves proud of having lived his dream and thanked the people who stood by him along the way. He signed off with a simple message to the game itself: "Thank you, football, for making me so happy."

Pedro moved to Barcelona from Tenerife at 17 and rose through the club's youth system and Barça B before making his first-team debut in the 2007/08 season. He signed his first senior contract in 2009 and went on to become a key player in one of the most successful eras in the club's history. In more than a decade at Barcelona he made over 200 appearances and scored 99 goals, winning five La Liga titles, three Copa del Rey trophies and three Champions League crowns.

In 2015 he joined Chelsea, where he spent five years in the Premier League. He later played in Italy for Roma and Lazio, leaving Lazio this summer when his contract ended.

For Spain, Pedro won 65 caps between 2010 and 2017 and was part of the golden generation that won the 2010 World Cup in South Africa and the 2012 European Championship.

Reflecting on his time at Barcelona, he said being part of the best Barça in history was a privilege, and that his heart will always be a Barça fan's. The club responded that he will always be part of its history.

Barcelona will mark his retirement with a farewell event this Friday, 9 October, at the Auditori 1899, starting at 11:30am CEST.

articles.title: Kibabii University Closed Indefinitely After Student Dies in Night Attack, Sparking Protests
articles.summary: Senate suspends first semester and orders all students to vacate as unrest grips the Bungoma institution.
articles.body:
BUNGOMA, October 6, 2026. Kibabii University has been closed indefinitely and learning suspended after violent student protests triggered by the reported death of a student in a night attack.

Students took to the streets on Tuesday morning after news spread that one of their colleagues had died following an attack on Monday night. According to reports, unknown assailants attacked four students near the university, leaving one dead and three others injured.

Classes boycotted, protests turn tense

The demonstrations escalated as students boycotted classes and poured out of the campus, disrupting normal activities at the institution. Details of the clashes remain limited, and it is unclear whether there were arrests or further injuries during the protests.

University shuts down

By afternoon, the university's Senate had convened a special meeting and resolved to suspend all first-semester activities for the 2026/2027 academic year with immediate effect.

In a memo, the university directed all students to vacate the premises immediately. Those living in university hostels were ordered to leave by 3pm on Tuesday. The institution has been closed indefinitely, with no date given for reopening.

Unanswered questions

The university has not yet publicly explained the circumstances of the attack. The identity of the deceased student, the exact location of the incident, the motive and the condition of the injured students had not been confirmed at the time of publishing, and no suspects have been announced.

The closure comes at a difficult time for higher education in Kenya. Public universities across the country are already grappling with disruption following a nationwide lecturers' strike that began on Friday, October 2.

This is a developing story and will be updated as police and the university release more information.

articles.title: Kenya Confirms First Ebola Case as Patient Who Travelled from DRC Dies in Nairobi
articles.summary: Health officials say the patient passed airport screening before being rushed to hospital, as the country moves to step up surveillance.
articles.body:
NAIROBI, October 6, 2026. Kenya has recorded its first confirmed case of Ebola, and the patient has died, Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale announced on Tuesday.

The patient, a Kenyan citizen who had lived in the Democratic Republic of Congo for seven years, was infected with the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, a rare and often fatal form of Ebola disease. He is the first person in Kenya to be diagnosed with the illness.

A long journey home

According to the Ministry of Health, the man fell ill about a month ago and was treated at several hospitals in the DRC. He then travelled by road to Kampala, Uganda, where he boarded a Jambojet flight to Nairobi, arriving on Saturday.

At Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, he underwent the standard health screening conducted by Port Health officers and cleared immigration. A relative and a friend then drove him directly to Nairobi Hospital.

Isolated on arrival

Doctors at the hospital suspected a viral haemorrhagic fever and isolated him immediately. Samples taken from the patient tested positive for Ebola. Despite supportive treatment, he died at 11:30 pm on Monday.

The Ministry said his burial would take place on Tuesday, in line with Ebola safety protocols, which strictly control how the bodies of victims are handled to prevent further infection.

Government response

The ministry has activated its national Ebola incident management system, with contact tracing, border surveillance and coordination with neighbouring countries under way. Kenya has also notified the World Health Organization of the case, as required under the International Health Regulations.

The case comes as the DRC battles a major Bundibugyo outbreak that was declared in May. Kenya is now among a small number of countries outside the DRC to have recorded a case linked to it.

Questions over screening

The patient's journey is likely to raise questions about how effective airport screening is at detecting travellers who have been ill for weeks. Authorities have indicated that the patient's condition may not have been obvious at the point of entry.

What the public should know

Health authorities generally advise people to:

Wash hands regularly with soap and water or use sanitiser.
Avoid contact with the blood or bodily fluids of anyone who is sick.
Seek medical care immediately if they develop fever, severe fatigue, muscle pain or unexplained bleeding after travel from an affected area, and tell the health worker about that travel history.
Rely on official Ministry of Health updates rather than unverified social media posts.

articles.title: Ruto Promises Teachers Housing Check-Off, 50,000 Promotions and 20,000 Permanent Jobs on World Teachers' Day
articles.summary: NAIROBI, October 5, 2026: President William Ruto used this year's World Teachers' Day celebrations to announce a series of measures on housing, jobs, promotions and pay. The celebrations were held at Kasarani in Nairobi under the theme "Standing with teachers," with teachers, TSC officials, MPs and Ministry of Education officials in attendance.
articles.body:
Housing: pay for a home straight from your salary

The headline announcement was on housing. Ruto said the Affordable Housing Board is working with the Teachers Service Commission on a check-off system that will let teachers pay for their homes directly from their salaries, and that applicants can apply through the Boma Yangu platform. He repeated that the government had committed to reserving 20% of affordable homes for teachers, and said it is working with teachers' unions on financing tailored to their incomes. 

The details are still missing. Ruto did not give the interest rates, repayment periods or eligibility requirements for the proposed financing. The 20 per cent reservation comes from an agreement signed in September 2025 between the Affordable Housing Board, KNUT and KUPPET.

Jobs and promotions

On recruitment, Ruto said the government had hired 100,000 teachers over the past four years and would recruit another 20,000 before the end of 2026, bringing the total to 120,000 by December. He also announced a KSh4.9 billion plan to move 20,000 contract teachers to permanent and pensionable terms from January 2027. 

On career progression, Ruto said 50,000 teachers will be promoted this financial year, after the promotion budget was doubled from KSh1 billion to KSh2 billion. He said new career progression guidelines agreed by the TSC and unions are awaiting approval by the Salaries and Remuneration Commission. 

Pay and benefits

Ruto again addressed the unions' demand for a shorter pay-review cycle. He said reducing the Collective Bargaining Agreement cycle from four years to two will be considered once the current 2025–2029 agreement ends, and that the 2026/2027 budget includes an extra KSh8.1 billion to keep the agreement on schedule. The promise follows one made a year ago at State House, where he asked the TSC, the ministry and unions to propose a suitable period. 

On health cover, he said that as of September 2026 the Social Health Authority covers 415,608 teachers and 884,392 dependants. On retirement, he said the government is working to pay retirement benefits faster, with teachers' records currently being uploaded into the system.

A message on exams

Ruto also spoke to the profession about the coming national examinations. He urged teachers to prepare candidates well while protecting the integrity of the process, warning that certificates obtained through cheating would undermine the value of qualifications. He added that a teacher's contribution should not be judged by exam grades alone. 

Context

TSC chairman Muturi said Ruto is the first president since 1963 to join teachers in marking the day. That is the chairman's claim, and I haven't independently checked it. Most of the figures in this story are the president's own and have not been independently verified. Several of the commitments, including the check-off system, the new guidelines and the shorter CBA cycle, are still promises or awaiting approval.

articles.title: From Raw Data to Real Insights: How Data Analysis Works
articles.summary: Every day, businesses, hospitals, schools and governments collect more data than they can read. The data alone doesn't help anyone. What helps is the process that turns it into a decision. Here are the stages, using one running example: a Nairobi retailer trying to understand why sales dropped last quarter.
articles.body:
1. Start with the question

Good analysis begins before any data is touched. The question must be specific and measurable. "Why are we doing badly?" is too vague. "Which products and which branches caused the 12% drop in revenue between July and September?" is something you can answer.

At this stage the analyst also agrees with the decision-maker on what success looks like and what action the answer could trigger. If no decision depends on the answer, the question isn't worth analysing.

2. Collect the data

Next comes finding the data that can answer the question. Sources vary:

Internal records: sales systems, M-Pesa transaction logs, inventory sheets, customer databases.
Surveys and interviews: useful when the answer is about opinions or behaviour that no system records.
Public data: statistics from government agencies such as the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics, central bank data, open data portals.
Digital sources: website analytics, social media, app usage.

Collection decisions shape everything after them. A biased sample, a badly worded survey question or a missing branch will mislead the analysis, and no technique can fix that later. Analysts also need permission to use the data and a plan to protect personal information, which in Kenya means following the Data Protection Act.

3. Clean and prepare the data

This stage takes most of an analyst's time, often well over half, and it is the least glamorous. Raw data is almost always messy:

Duplicate records, such as the same sale entered twice.
Missing values, such as a branch that didn't report for two weeks.
Inconsistent formats, such as "Nairobi", "NAIROBI" and "nbi" in the same column, or dates written three different ways.
Impossible values, such as a negative quantity or a price of KSh 0.
Outliers, which may be real (a bulk order) or errors (an extra zero).

Each fix is a judgment call. Delete the row, fill the gap with an estimate, or go back and ask the person who recorded it? The key habit is to keep a record of every change so the work can be checked and repeated. Tools range from Excel and Google Sheets to Python (pandas), R and SQL.

4. Explore the data

Before testing anything, the analyst looks. Exploratory analysis means summarising and charting the data to see what's in it: averages and spreads, how values are distributed, how variables move together, and where the surprises are.

In the retailer example, a simple chart of monthly sales by branch might show that one branch collapsed in August while the others only dipped slightly. That immediately narrows the search. Exploration doesn't prove anything, but it guides what to test next.

5. Analyse and model

Now the analyst applies methods that fit the question:

Descriptive analysis answers "what happened?" with totals, averages and trends.
Diagnostic analysis answers "why?" by comparing groups, checking correlations and running statistical tests.
Predictive analysis answers "what is likely next?" using regression or machine learning models.
Prescriptive analysis answers "what should we do?" by comparing the likely outcomes of different actions.

The method should be as simple as the question allows. A clear comparison of two groups often beats a complicated model that nobody can explain. Analysts also check that the result is statistically meaningful and not just chance, and they remember that correlation is not causation. Ice cream sales and drowning both rise in hot months, but one doesn't cause the other.

6. Interpret the results

Numbers don't speak for themselves. Interpretation means connecting the findings back to the original question and asking whether they make sense in the real world. Do they agree with what people on the ground say? Could something that wasn't measured explain them?

In the example, the analysis might show the August collapse was at the branch where a competitor opened across the road, and that the loss was concentrated in one product line. That is a finding. It becomes an insight when it points to an action, such as reviewing prices on that line or running a loyalty offer at that branch.

7. Communicate the insights

The best analysis fails if the audience doesn't understand it. Good communication means:

Leading with the answer, then showing the evidence.
Choosing simple charts that make one point each.
Using plain language instead of technical terms.
Being honest about limits: what the data can't tell us and how confident the analyst is.
Ending with clear recommendations.

Dashboards, short reports and presentations all work, as long as they are built around the decision the audience has to make.

8. Act, monitor and repeat

Analysis doesn't end with the report. Once a decision is made, the same metrics should be tracked to see whether it worked. If the loyalty offer doesn't bring customers back, that is new data, and the cycle starts again with a sharper question.

The takeaway

Data analysis is a loop: question, collect, clean, explore, analyse, interpret, communicate, act. The technical tools matter, but the habits matter more: starting with a clear question, respecting data quality, staying honest about uncertainty, and explaining results in a way people can act on.

articles.title: Sifuna Unveils The Equitable Party, Says It Will Become Linda Mwananchi and Accuses Registrar of Fraud
articles.summary: Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's party, The Equitable Party (TEP), was unveiled at a ceremony in Nairobi, with Sifuna presented as party leader and presidential flagbearer for the 2027 general election. The launch was a workaround. The movement's preferred name, Linda Mwananchi, is still not a registered part
articles.body:
A borrowed vehicle.
TEP leader Gilbert Marava confirmed that Sifuna would lead the party and be its 2027 presidential candidate. Caroli Omondi told the crowd the formation would be led by a single presidential candidate and that its members would stand united behind Sifuna.

The turnout showed the strength of the Linda Mwananchi coalition. Those present included Siaya Governor James Orengo, Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, Senators Godfrey Osotsi, Richard Onyonka and Boni Khalwale, and MPs including Babu Owino and Caroli Omondi.

Why TEP, and why the rebrand

TEP is a fallback after months of obstruction. The Office of the Registrar of Political Parties (ORPP) declined the movement's application for the Linda Mwananchi name, citing similarity to another outfit using the acronym LINDA. The dispute went to the tribunal. On September 30 the Political Parties Disputes Tribunal set aside the rejection, calling it unconstitutional and noting that the LINDA reservation had lapsed. The reports add that a rival claim by Charles Wanyonyi's Linda Mwananchi Party of Kenya, filed in February 2026, still creates administrative hurdles. 
Profile Of The Equitable Party, Edwin Sifuna's Platform For The 2027 Elections

Sifuna said the rebrand would come soon. He told supporters that, as resolved by the Linda Mwananchi principals present, the movement would seek to rename the party the Linda Mwananchi Movement in the coming days. The name is protected for now but not yet secured: it has been reserved for 90 days, which gives its promoters time to meet the remaining requirements, though a reservation is not registration.

Not everyone is treating the launch as the main event. Osotsi said Sunday's event was mainly to announce the party the movement is adopting, with a bigger Linda Mwananchi launch to come, though he gave no date.

"Registrar facilitates fraud"

The sharpest moment of the day was Sifuna's attack on the registrar. He accused the ORPP of facilitating political fraud. The allegation was made at the launch, and the reports I found do not show the registrar's response. The ORPP has the right to reply, and a published version of this story should seek its comment.

He also said there is a fallback if the rebrand stalls. If efforts to rename the party run into further obstacles, the formation will carry on under The Equitable Party name. He added that a team of experts is finalising the movement's policy platform for the 2027 election.

Decoys

Khalwale offered a more strategic account of the registration saga. He said the movement deliberately floated several political parties as "decoys" to confuse President William Ruto's camp and protect Sifuna's real vehicle. This is Khalwale's claim and has not been independently verified. It does suggest the allies see the paperwork fight as part of the campaign.

Background

The launch ends Sifuna's search for a political home after he was removed as Orange Democratic Movement Secretary General. Last week, after a leadership retreat, the movement's leaders resolved to end their differences and back him as leader and presidential candidate. TEP, in his words, is the vehicle for sending President Ruto home. 
Sifuna unveils The Equitable Party as his 2027 vehicle.

The party now has two parallel tasks: building TEP as its immediate vehicle while pursuing the Linda Mwananchi rebrand within the statutory requirements. The 90-day reservation clock, the rival Wanyonyi application, and the registrar's response to the fraud claim will decide whether the Linda Mwananchi name survives to 2027.

articles.title: Gachagua alleges late Zimbabwean tycoon Chivayo held KSh1.5 trillion for Ruto, offers no evidence
articles.summary: Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that the businessman killed in a Zimbabwe helicopter crash was holding money for President Ruto. He did not produce evidence, and the claim is unproven.
articles.body:
Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has alleged that late Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo was holding more than KSh1.5 trillion belonging to President William Ruto when he died. He made the claims while speaking to clergy in Boston, in the United States, without providing evidence for them. The remarks were made on Sunday, October 4, 2026.

According to Gachagua, Chivayo was used to move and store money for the President, and he alleged that dollars were flown by plane to private airstrips. The figure he cited, KSh1.5 trillion, is equivalent to about US$11 billion. He also accused the President of having stolen the money and linked Chivayo to his earlier allegations about the procurement of election technology ahead of the 2027 General Election. 
Gachagua Claims Chivayo Held KSh1.5 Trillion for Ruto.

One report noted that there is no independent evidence showing that Chivayo held such funds for Ruto, and that neither the President nor his representatives had publicly responded to the allegation when it was published. 

Chivayo and his wife, Lucy Muteke, were among six people killed when a helicopter crashed in Marondera, Zimbabwe, on the evening of Wednesday, September 30. Zimbabwe's Civil Aviation Authority said preliminary observations showed that the helicopter hit the ground, spilling fuel that ignited, and investigators have begun examining what caused it to go down. No cause has been announced. 
arkansasonline

After the crash, President Ruto mourned Chivayo, whom he called a "dear friend," and sent condolences to the bereaved families. The two were known to be close, with Chivayo a frequent sight at State House and national events. Kenyan opposition figures had earlier questioned his repeated access to Ruto and State House. 
President Ruto mourns ‘Dear Friend’ Wicknell Chivayo killed in chopper crash.

The allegation adds to Gachagua's wider criticism of the President. In August he accused Ruto of capturing the state and using the presidency to enrich himself. The government has not been shown to have responded to the Chivayo claim, so this story will be updated if it does.

articles.title: Why every business needs a website, from the roadside shop to the growing company
articles.summary: Social media pages are useful, but a website gives a business credibility, visibility and a place it fully controls. Here is why it matters.
articles.body:
Many small businesses in Kenya start on WhatsApp and social media, and that works well at the beginning. The problem comes when a business wants to grow. Social pages belong to the platform, their reach can change overnight, and they don't show up in a search the way a proper website does.

A website works as a shop front that never closes. A customer searching on their phone late at night can find your services, prices and location without waiting for a reply. For many shoppers, a business with a website simply looks more established than one without.

Search is the second big reason. When someone types what they need into Google, a website with clear, useful pages gives your business a chance to appear. A social media profile rarely gets that same visibility, and every visitor who finds you through search is a customer you didn't have to chase.

A website also lets you own your audience. You decide the layout, the message and the contact details, and you can collect enquiries directly without depending on an algorithm. It can also take payments. Sites can connect to M-Pesa through Safaricom's Daraja API, so customers can pay for orders or bookings on the spot.

Finally, a website gives you information. Simple analytics show how many people visit, which pages they read and where they come from, so you can improve your services based on real behaviour instead of guesses.

You don't need a large budget to start. A small business can begin with a simple, mobile-friendly site that has a clear description of what it does, its prices or packages, a contact page and a map, then add features as it grows. The key is to choose a site that can grow with the business, so you aren't forced to rebuild later.

articles.title: Opposition chiefs vow to field one candidate at Karua family burial
articles.summary: The burial of Mwalimu Jackson Karua, father of PLP leader Martha Karua, on Saturday, October 3, 2026, became more than a family farewell as leading opposition figures shared a platform in Gichugu, Kirinyaga County
articles.body:
Kalonzo Musyoka, Fred Matiang'i, Edwin Sifuna, Justin Muturi, Ndindi Nyoro, Eugene Wamalwa and Martha Karua declared that they would unite and field one presidential candidate to face President Ruto. They accused him of abetting corruption and running down the economy, and promised to make him a one-term president. Retired President Uhuru Kenyatta and Siaya Governor James Orengo were also present. 
Uhuru to Mt Kenya: Electing Ruto in 2022 was a mistake, repeating it in 2027 would be worse +2

Kenyatta told the leaders to take the Kirinyaga Woman Representative's call for unity and a single presidential candidate seriously. 

Matiang'i urged opposition leaders to be honest with one another as they seek a joint candidate, warning against appearing united in public while pursuing different positions elsewhere. Sifuna raised the one-ticket question, while Orengo focused on Mt Kenya numbers. 

The opposition has already committed to this. At an earlier sitting on August 24, the united opposition leaders signed a vow to rally behind one candidate despite all of them having presidential ambitions. A technical committee has prepared a manual on how they will choose a flagbearer, but the timing of unveiling the candidate remains unresolved.

articles.title: Uganda's army chief Muhoozi backs Ruto for a second term and names Wetang'ula his "Mutume" in Kenya
articles.summary: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces, has publicly endorsed President Ruto's 2027 re-election bid, drawing a regional voice into Kenya's campaign debate.
articles.body:
Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has openly backed President William Ruto's 2027 re-election bid. He made the declaration in a post on X on Friday, October 2, naming National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula as his political "Mutume" in Kenya. The word is understood in the context of the post to mean an emissary or representative. 

In the post, he wrote that Wetang'ula would support Ruto's re-election and ended with the line "Tunataka Second term," meaning "we want a second term." Reports say Muhoozi clarified that his statements are not an official endorsement by the Ugandan government. The post also did not indicate that Wetang'ula had received any formal appointment or role in Ruto's campaign. 
Regional intrigue as Uganda’s Military Chief Gen. Muhoozi backs Ruto for 2027 re-election +2

Wetang'ula has been stepping up his own mobilisation for Ruto. He said he reminded people in the region that he was once a fierce defender of Raila Odinga, and this time urged them to rally behind the president's bid and stay in the broad-based government. 
peopledaily

Muhoozi is President Museveni's son and the head of the Ugandan army. He is widely seen as being groomed for the Ugandan presidency and is known for direct and controversial social media posts. In October 2022, shortly after Ruto took office, he caused a diplomatic row by suggesting on X that his forces could capture Nairobi in under two weeks. President Museveni apologised to Ruto and Kenya, and Muhoozi was later promoted to full general. 

Observers describe the latest post as an unusually direct intervention by a senior Ugandan military officer in a neighbouring country's election politics. It comes as Kenyan parties, emerging movements and individual politicians explore alliances aimed at making Ruto a one-term president. 

We have not seen a response to the post from Ruto's office or the Kenyan government.

articles.title: The rise of Edwin Sifuna: from ODM secretary-general to opposition presidential contender
articles.summary: Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has moved from running ODM's party machinery to leading a new political movement backed for the 2027 presidential race.
articles.body:
Edwin Sifuna, a lawyer, was named secretary-general of the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) on 23 February 2018, replacing Ababu Namwamba. In August 2022 he won the Nairobi Senate seat, defeating Bishop Margaret Wanjiru. 

His profile grew most after the death of ODM leader Raila Odinga and ODM's cooperation deal with President William Ruto's government. Sifuna became the face of resistance inside the party by openly criticising the agreement with the government and insisting ODM should remain a full opposition party. 
nation

That stance cost him his party post. The Registrar of Political Parties approved his removal as secretary-general, saying it followed the Political Parties Act and ODM's constitution. One account lists his time in the post as running until 9 July 2026. 

Outside the party, support was already forming. Linda Mwananchi leaders from Western Kenya announced plans for a new party and said they would put Sifuna forward for president. The Linda Mwananchi Movement later endorsed him as its presidential candidate after a retreat attended by several senior figures. 

The movement has faced legal hurdles. The Political Parties Disputes Tribunal set aside the Registrar's August 7 refusal to reserve the name, and in a letter dated October 1, 2026 the Registrar approved the application. The name is reserved for 90 days, and the movement must use that window to become an actual political organisation. Rival applications for similar names have also emerged. 

This week he has also taken on the government directly. He demanded in the Senate that Parliament be shown the agreement behind the proposed Dangote refinery in Lamu, and later cited Article 35 of the Constitution on access to information. President Ruto accused him of seeking the document outside Parliament, called him an extortionist, and said it should be requested through parliamentary procedures. On October 3 at a burial in Kirinyaga, Sifuna asked Mt Kenya residents to help settle who should carry the opposition ticket in 2027. 
Sifuna warns against secretive deals amid Dangote Oil Refinery row - People Daily +2

Whether the rise continues depends on registration deadlines and on whether the opposition agrees on a single candidate.

Sources: Nation, Citizen Digital, People Daily, Wikipedia.

articles.title: Gachagua says he is now aiming for State House in 2027, after earlier talk of backing Ruto to 2032
articles.summary: A headline circulating online quotes Rigathi Gachagua saying he once pledged to back President Ruto until 2032 but now expects to become president in 2027.
articles.body:
A statement attributed to former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua is drawing attention online. According to a headline circulating on social media, he said he had promised to support President William Ruto until 2032 but now expects to be president in 2027.

The remark appears alongside a video on Gachagua's official Facebook page, captioned "Through Partnership with the Diaspora, we shall bridge the gap on employment." The caption points to the diaspora and jobs as themes of the event. The exact wording of the quote, and where and when it was said, should be confirmed from the original video.

Gachagua announced on September 14, 2025, in Nyeri that he would run for president in 2027. By January 2026, as Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader, he was touring the Mt Kenya region and repeating that Ruto should serve only one term. In July 2026 he also said he would step aside for another candidate if that was what it took to unite the opposition and remove Ruto. 
'No lies, no false promises': Gachagua launches bid to unseat Ruto +2

The 2032 claim has been disputed before. During the 2022 campaign, Gachagua said his arrangement with Ruto was a five-year performance contract and that he had not agreed to back Ruto after his ten-year term. Later, a Mt Kenya politician, Mr Wamumbi, said he had personally advised Gachagua to submit to Ruto's presidency until 2032 before pursuing his own ambitions. 
peopledaily
nation

Allies of President Ruto have consistently downplayed opposition unification efforts, expressing confidence in the government's record and its prospects in 2027. 
peopledaily

Source: Gachagua's official Facebook page and published reports.

articles.title: KICC lit up in tribute to Raila Odinga as ODM opens "Mwezi wa Baba"
articles.summary: The Kenyatta International Convention Centre in Nairobi glowed with a tribute to the late former Prime Minister on Friday night, as ODM began a month of remembrance events.
articles.body:
Nairobi's Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) became a canvas for a light display honouring the late former Prime Minister Raila Odinga on Friday evening, while supporters in other parts of the country held remembrance events of their own.

The projection formed part of a countrywide candle-lighting led by the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM), which kicked off its October programme, named "Mwezi wa Baba", in memory of Raila, widely known as Baba.

Clips posted on ODM's official X account showed a glowing image of Raila circling the landmark tower, with the words "Baba Raila Odinga" displayed near the top of the building.

Source: videos shared on ODM's official X account.
